takeaway: The popliteal fossa floor is the popliteal surface of the femur, the knee joint capsule and the oblique popliteal ligament; the roof is deep fascia.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the popliteal fossa is correct?

answer.text: The floor contains the oblique popliteal ligament.

lines.text: The popliteal fossa is the diamond-shaped space at the back of the knee joint.
Semitendinosus forms the upper medial border,
and biceps femoris the upper lateral one.
Below, the two heads of gastrocnemius close the diamond.
The floor is the femur and the knee capsule,
and the oblique popliteal ligament, our answer.
Inside run the popliteal artery and vein, and the tibial and common peroneal nerves.
